stories.title: Nepal-Tibet floods: 72 Malaysians safe in China, 55 in Nepal still missing
stories.summary: A total of 55 Malaysians remain uncontactable in Nepal following severe flash floods that struck the country on Aug 26, said Malaysia’s Foreign Ministry. The Ministry said another 36 Malaysians have also been reported as uncontactable in China due to telecommunications disruptions. “In Nepal, 55 Malaysians remain reported as uncontactable, while two Malaysians previously reported as uncontactable have since been contacted. “Search and rescue operations and verification efforts remain ongoing, with no Malaysians identified at this stage among the 116 foreign nationals officially reported as rescued,” it said in a statement on Aug 29. The Ministry said it has also expanded its consular response beyond Nepal to assist Malaysians affected by related travel disruptions in China. “A group of 72 Malaysians in Darchen, China, has been confirmed safe and is receiving consular assistance from the Malaysian Embassy in Beijing. “Separately, information has been received regarding 36 Malaysians currently reported as uncontactable in areas affected by telecommunications disruptions in China. “The Ministry is working with the Chinese authorities and family members to establish contact, while cross-checking these reports against cases involving Malaysians in Nepal to identify any duplication,” it said. The Ministry added that its operations room continues to operate around the clock as efforts to establish the safety and whereabouts of the Malaysians concerned continue.

stories.title: Major Bangkok blaze hits 300 stalls in Khlong Thom, injures 11 amid toxic smoke alert
stories.summary: Hazardous smoke continued to rise from the collapsed remains of Khlong Thom Centre on the morning of Aug 29, after a major fire left 11 people injured and damaged hundreds of retail stalls in central Bangkok. Bangkok Governor Chadchart Sittipunt said firefighters were continuing to spray water around the ruins to prevent the blaze from reigniting. Smouldering material remained trapped beneath the collapsed structure, making it difficult for water to reach some areas. Excavators had been prepared overnight, but engineers were due to assess whether the machinery could be used safely to clear a route into the building and allow crews to locate the suspected source of the fire. The surrounding structure remained at risk of further collapse, requiring all operations to proceed cautiously. Shop owners and employees waiting to inspect the damage were not allowed to enter because parts of the building were leaning and remained unstable. The Bangkok Metropolitan Administration’s Erawan Emergency Medical Centre reported 11 injuries. One volunteer firefighter was in critical condition after inhaling smoke, while another person was classified as requiring urgent care. Nine others sustained minor injuries. Chadchart said the critically injured patient required intubation. Most of those hurt were volunteers, while one member of the public was treated for smoke inhalation. No deaths were reported and no one was believed to have been trapped inside.
